Ram 1500 SRT Gets Into the Slammed Widebody Street Mood, Though Only Across Fantasy Land
7 photos
Photo: trapndeth / Instagram
Ram Trucks is having a period of grace – they subdued Jeep and stole its crown as Stellantis’ best-selling brand in America not long ago and also launched a series of great pickup trucks, all based on one simple thing, which is the return of the Hemi V8 under the hood of the Ram 1500 models.
Just recently, the 2027 Ram 1500 Rumble Bee also got a Foose Edition just in time for the 2026 SEMA Show in Las Vegas, Nevada, and rode low on the red carpet with 1,000 hp laid to the ground. In Europe, Ram is launching the Rampage, at long last, as their mid-size-like option for a fashionable lifestyle, with two versions, each with its dedicated powertrain.
Let’s also not forget about the return of the mighty 2027 Ram 1500 TRX SRT, which recently encountered a Ford F-150 Raptor R and proved which one is the faster truck. Fans certainly appreciate the credentials, shared with the Rumble Bee SRT model – the 6.2-liter supercharged Hemi V8 used in the previous iteration now makes no less than 777 hp and 680 lb-ft of torque or 922 Nm, backing the 720-hp Ford F-150 Raptor R into a corner and reclaiming the crown of high-performance ICE adventure trucks.
The Ram 1500 SRT TRX celebrated the relaunch of the Street and Racing Technology (SRT) division when it was unveiled on January 1, 2026, and since then has quietly amassed its ‘super’ power for the off-road adventures that lie ahead. But what if someone wants it on the street and only on the street?
Many would say that you just need to catch a 2027 Ram 1500 Rumble Bee SRT instead. However, that’s still not enough for some folks – especially a member of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators dwelling across the parallel universes of vehicular CGI. More precisely, TRAPNDETH, the virtual artist who wants to "trap death to stay alive" (aka " trapndeth " on social media), has created a slammed widebody truck for the ages – an SRT with the Ram looks and the allure of a Fast & Furious build.
Instead of sporting off-road credentials like the Ram 1500 TRX SRT or mild street allure like the Rumble Bee, it goes full throttle with the CGI and slams itself into the ground so hard that it becomes flatter and wider at the same time. As such, it now has a complete widebody aerodynamic kit featuring a new front with a massive lip spoiler, a muscular hood, sculpted fender flares, a new rear with an integrated bed cover and ducktail spoiler, as well as a massive diffuser.
Around the sides are new side ‘steps’ and also massive-lipped alloy wheels, signaling that this build is ready for cool things both on the street and at the track. You won’t be doing much hauling or off-roading with it, since the stance is taking it as close as possible to the ground – so much so that even an ant would fear for its life when seeing that massive front spoiler. So, what do you think – yay or nay? View this post on Instagram A post shared by TRAPNDETH (@trapndeth)
